experiment: E112b (Q133): the card-1 view of Q132(r)'s frozen file
what: FROZEN predictions and claims for the real2 tiles, made before any card ran them: (a) D at 600 MHz on aifoundry3 (E95) from Q130(n)'s frozen predictor with an interval fitted on its known out-of-sample misses; (a') its offset from a partner tile; (b) the burst and sustained clock under aifoundry2's own governor (E96) from E83's relation; (c) the gate law for gated tiles, separately; and the claims E95 and E96 test.

predictor.note: unchanged. E90's correction binds: it tracks a re-draw's offset from a measured tile (0.28 W rms) and misses absolute prices by 0.6-2.0 W; the intervals below say so, and it is a post-hoc fit, not a mechanism

known_misses.definition: measured D minus Q130(n)'s frozen point, W, tiles the predictor was not fitted on

int8_gated.note: no E86 or E90 tile gates in int8, so this class uses E78's nested-LOO out-of-fold residuals (tools/claims-v3/kinds/real/amendment-1.json nested_loo.int8.nested_residual_w), measured minus predicted; flagged as the one class not fitted on E86/E90

gate_law.form: D = g G + (1 - g) L; g = the tile's computed gated_lane_frac (make_kinds.tile_stats); no fitted parameter

relation_e83.interval: the clock at the ends of the (a) scoring interval, widened in quadrature by 1.96 x relation rms, clamped to [600, 800]; a range wholly at the cap stays [800, 800] (Amendment 1's rule)
relation_e83.e87_note: E87 read this relation on real tiles: 10.7 / 6.1 MHz rms frozen; its session's heat path ran 0.5 C warmer than E80's, and single int8 sustained runs land either side of the 65 C trip whatever the data

e95_suggested.items: the 25 new tier-1 tiles as <type>.r2_<name>, E86's fp16.real_l6_mlp_down and int8.real_l6_mlp_down, E78's six anchors three times a pass, the anchor_pi tie twice: 47 runs and 2 burn-ins a pass
e95_suggested.estimate: E86 ran 32 runs and 2 burn-ins in 6.0-6.7 min, about 12 s a run, so 49 runs is about 10 min a pass and four passes about 40 card-minutes, with the smoke inside the 45; tier 2 adds 5 runs, about 1 min a pass

e96_suggested.bursts: every tier-1 tile and E87's six anchors, two passes
e96_suggested.why: 27 tiles in E87's full shape is about 75 card-minutes (E87: 13 s a burst, 100 s a sustained run). The ungated float tiles are predicted at random data's clock, so their sustained runs say least

c_if_gate_took_numeric_zero.note: the gate as built tests word == 0, so -0.0 passes; this is what the law says if it did not

claims.conventions: All energy claims are on D, each tile's board power over its own type's all-zeros level, at the E95 lane's primary leakage slope, on aifoundry3 at 600 MHz. r(x) = per pass D(x) / D(ref), ref the same pass's fp32.randn, fp16.randn or int8.full (its three runs' mean). Intervals are t(0.975, n - 1) x SE over kept passes; a difference is paired within the pass. PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE as each claim says. Fewer than 3 kept passes: NOT SCORED. A lane that drops a tile says so, and a claim short of its population is UNDER-RESOLVED, never PASS.

C1_within_2pct.claim: Real fp32 and fp16 tiles with no exact zeros cost within 2% of random data of their format over its zeros, in every model
C1_within_2pct.rule: per cell, mean r over its tiles per pass, its 95% interval over passes: cell PASS if inside the band, FAIL if entirely outside, else INCONCLUSIVE. Claim PASS if every cell passes, FAIL if any fails, else INCONCLUSIVE
C1_within_2pct.how_it_can_fail: an attention tile in fp16 already read 0.971 and 0.966 (E86, E91), below the band; a model whose numbers sit further from random fails it

C2_below_random.claim: On average real fp32 and fp16 tiles with no exact zeros sit below random data of their format
C2_below_random.rule: per format, mean r over its N tiles per pass: PASS if the 95% upper bound < 1, FAIL if the lower bound > 1, else INCONCLUSIVE (E86-R3's form). Both formats must pass

C3a_live_share_tiles.claim: A ReLU tile's power follows its live share: each fp32 and fp16 ReLU tile lies inside the gate law's interval
C3a_live_share_tiles.rule: count of tiles whose D lies inside c_gate_law.scoring_interval_w: PASS if all, FAIL if two or more lie outside, else INCONCLUSIVE
C3a_live_share_tiles.law: D = g G + (1 - g) L, gate_law.<type>

C3b_live_share_slope.claim: Across the ReLU tiles of a format, D rises with the live share at about the random kind's full cost
C3b_live_share_slope.rule: per format, the least-squares slope of D on (1 - g) over its tiles, divided by E78's L: PASS if both formats lie inside the band, FAIL if either lies outside
C3b_live_share_slope.known: the same slope over E78's gated kinds and E90's gated re-draws: gate_law.<type>.known_misses

C4_word_grouping.claim: The same numbers cost more in fp16 than in fp32 because a zero must fill the whole 32-bit word
C4_word_grouping.rule: per pair, r(fp16) - r(fp32), paired: PASS if the 95% lower bound > 0, FAIL if the upper bound < 0, else INCONCLUSIVE. Claim PASS if all three pass, FAIL if any fails

C5_int8_bits_or_gate.claim: In int8 a real ReLU tile's power follows its operand bits more than its live share: the predictor (a) lies nearer the measurement than the gate law (c)
C5_int8_bits_or_gate.rule: per tile, |D - (a)| against |D - (c)|: PASS if (a) is nearer on both tiles, FAIL if (c) is nearer on both, else INCONCLUSIVE
C5_int8_bits_or_gate.why_this_side: E78's int8 sparse50 gates 7% of its lane-cycles and its saving follows its bits; E86's real int8 tiles cost 0.78-0.89 of full with no gate at all

C6_calibration_lever.claim: On a GELU layer with one huge activation the calibration is a lever several times larger than any data effect: 99.9th percentile clip against max-abs
C6_calibration_lever.rule: paired D difference: PASS if the 95% lower bound >= 2.0 W, FAIL if the upper bound < 2.0 W, else INCONCLUSIVE

C7_calibration_rank.claim: On E86's window the calibrations rank committed < per-token < 99.9th percentile by power; the 99.99th percentile clip sits beside committed
C7_calibration_rank.rule: paired differences against the reference: PASS if per-token's and 99.9th's lower bounds > 0 and p9999's interval lies inside +-0.40 W; FAIL if per-token's or 99.9th's upper bound < 0, or p9999's interval lies entirely outside +-0.40 W; else INCONCLUSIVE
C7_calibration_rank.note: the predicted steps are 0.04-0.24 W, at the size of E86's paired noise, so INCONCLUSIVE is the likely outcome; beside the verdict report Spearman over the four and each tile's r

C8_asym_turns_the_gate_off.claim: TFLite-style asymmetric activations show the gate nothing on a ReLU tile, so the same numbers cost more than the symmetric tile
C8_asym_turns_the_gate_off.rule: paired D difference: PASS if the 95% lower bound > 0.5 W, FAIL if the upper bound < 0, else INCONCLUSIVE

C9_negative_zero.claim: The gate tests word == 0, so -0.0 passes it: a tile whose A is 64% -0.0 (the layer: 55%) costs more than the gate law allows if the gate took numeric zeros

prediction_if_gate_took_numeric_zero.note: the gate as built tests word == 0, so -0.0 passes; this is what the law says if it did not

C9_negative_zero.rule: PASS if D's 95% lower bound > the upper end of c_if_gate_took_numeric_zero.scoring_interval_w, FAIL if D's 95% upper bound <= that end, else INCONCLUSIVE. Reported beside: r, which says what a live lane multiplying -0.0 costs

C10_bf16_weights.claim: T5's weights sit on the bf16 grid (all low 16 mantissa bits zero), so a no-zero T5 tile costs clearly less than random fp32, unlike E86's full-mantissa tiles
C10_bf16_weights.rule: r: PASS if the 95% upper bound < 0.97, FAIL if the lower bound >= 0.97, else INCONCLUSIVE

C11_fp16_forward.claim: An fp16 forward pass costs what rounding the fp32 activations costs
C11_fp16_forward.rule: paired D difference: PASS if the 95% interval lies inside +-0.50 W, FAIL if entirely outside, else INCONCLUSIVE

C12_intervals.population: the 25 new tier-1 tiles, and any tier-2 tile run, counted apart
C12_intervals.rule: count of new tier-1 tiles with D inside a_aifoundry3_600mhz.scoring_interval_w: PASS if >= 20 of 25, FAIL if < 18, else INCONCLUSIVE. Beside it, labelled: the count inside the E86-only arm; rms per class against the class's known rms; for the ungated float tiles the no-model baseline 'each tile costs E78's random kind'

S1_intervals.claim: E83's relation fed (a) holds the clocks
S1_intervals.rule: bursts: count inside b_aifoundry2_governor.burst_scoring_interval_mhz, sustained: count inside sus_scoring_interval_mhz; each PASS if >= 80% of the tiles run, FAIL if < 60%, else INCONCLUSIVE

S2_gate_buys_speed.claim: A gated float tile whose (a) is under 15 W bursts well above same-session random data of its format
S2_gate_buys_speed.rule: per tile, burst minus the same session's randn burst of its format: PASS if every tile >= +40 MHz, FAIL if any tile < +15 MHz, else INCONCLUSIVE

S2b_gate_buys_sustained_clock.claim: The same tiles also sustain well above same-session random data of their format
S2b_gate_buys_sustained_clock.rule: per tile, sustained minus the same session's randn sustained of its format: PASS if every tile >= +50 MHz, FAIL if any tile < +15 MHz, else INCONCLUSIVE. One sustained run's 1 sigma is +-15.6 MHz on the slope (E83 C3)

S3_no_zero_runs_at_random_speed.claim: Real fp32 and fp16 tiles with no exact zeros burst within 15 MHz of same-session randn (E87-S2's form)
S3_no_zero_runs_at_random_speed.rule: per format, the tiles' mean burst minus randn's: PASS if |difference| <= 15 MHz in both formats, FAIL otherwise

S4_limits.claim: The sustained limit is called right
S4_limits.rule: count of sus_limit right: PASS if >= 80% of the tiles run, FAIL if < 60%, else INCONCLUSIVE

S5_relation_on_measured_power.claim: E83's relation on each tile's measured c gives its clocks (E87-S1's form)
S5_relation_on_measured_power.rule: burst and sustained rms each <= 15 MHz: PASS; either > 25 MHz: FAIL; else INCONCLUSIVE

e112_card1_view.rule: every watt figure a frozen E95 claim reads, divided by E82's per-type card scale of the tile's type (Q130(n)'s Amendment 1 did the same for E91); ratios, live shares, bus counts, clocks and r thresholds unchanged; known_misses as frozen (reported only); C7's +-0.40 W and C8's 0.5 W, which score_e95.py writes in its code, added scaled as e112_threshold_w
e112_card1_view.excludes: the card-scale spread (E82's per-kind ratios: IQR 1.025-1.034 over 32 kinds; X3 FAIL)
e112_card1_view.b_aifoundry2_governor: aifoundry2's clock predictions are untouched and not used by E112
